title: Parse a log line
summary: Split a structured access-log line into its fields, and refuse lines that do not fit.
prompt: Your service writes one line per request:
Write `LogLine? Parse(string line)` that returns a `LogLine(DateTime At, string Level, string Method, string Path, int Status, int Ms)`.
- Fields are separated by **one or more spaces**; leading and trailing spaces are fine.
- `At` is the ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, parsed as UTC (`DateTimeKind.Utc`).
- `Ms` is the number before the `ms` suffix.

- Return `null` for anything that does not fit: the wrong number of fields, a status that is not a number, a duration without `ms`, a bad timestamp. **Never throw**: one bad line must not stop a log scan.
The record `LogLine` is already declared by the tests.
solution: if (!int.TryParse(parts[4], out var status)) return null;
if (!parts[5].EndsWith("ms") || !int.TryParse(parts[5][..^2], out var ms)) return null;
return new LogLine(at, parts[1], parts[2], parts[3], status, ms);
template: Dojo.Check("a good line parses", a is not null, "Parse returned null for a valid line");
Dojo.Eq("At is the right instant", new DateTime(2026, 11, 26, 9, 14, 3, DateTimeKind.Utc), a.At);
Dojo.Check("extra spaces are fine", Parse("  2026-11-26T09:14:03Z   WARN  POST /pay 502   1200ms ") is { Status: 502, Ms: 1200, Level: "WARN" }, "spaces between fields vary");
Dojo.Try("bad lines give null, never an exception", () =>
Dojo.Check("too few fields -> null", Parse("2026-11-26T09:14:03Z INFO GET") is null, "");
Dojo.Check("status not a number -> null", Parse("2026-11-26T09:14:03Z INFO GET / OK 3ms") is null, "");
Dojo.Check("duration without ms -> null", Parse("2026-11-26T09:14:03Z INFO GET / 200 3s") is null, "");
Dojo.Check("bad timestamp -> null", Parse("yesterday INFO GET / 200 3ms") is null, "");
Dojo.Check("empty line -> null", Parse("") is null, "");
record LogLine(DateTime At, string Level, string Method, string Path, int Status, int Ms);
wrong: return new LogLine(DateTime.Parse(parts[0]), parts[1], parts[2], parts[3], int.Parse(parts[4]), ms);
hints: Use the `TryParse` family so a bad field gives `false` instead of an exception.
`DateTimeStyles.AdjustToUniversal | DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal` keeps the instant in UTC.
